extracted.intended_audience: rOpenSci volunteer reviewers evaluating rOpenSci R package submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing open, constructive peer reviews of R packages submitted to rOpenSci, including what to check, how to check it, and procedural expectations for submitting and following up on reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Please strive to complete your review within 3 weeks of accepting a review request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will remind reviewers of upcoming and past due dates. Editors may assign additional or alternate reviewers if a review is excessively late. If you expect delays, contact the editor directly or in the submission thread to inform them about possible delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use latest submitted branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be based on the latest GitHub version on the default branch, unless otherwise indicated by package authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the package is not submitted via the default/main branch, remember to switch to the submitted review branch before starting your review. In that case you will also have to search the package locally, as GitHub search is limited to the default branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pkgcheck / generated package report
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions trigger a detailed report on package structure and functionality, generated by the pkgcheck package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the package has changed substantially since the last checks, you may request a re-check with the command '@ropensci-review-bot check package'. Reviewers should check the initial package report generated by @ropensci-review-bot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure dependencies available for installation
rubrics_metrics.description: When installing the package to review it, make sure you have all dependencies available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: run pak::pak() to ensure dependencies are installed so the package can be built and tested on your system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with the review template as checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by copying the review template and using it as a high-level checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to checking off the minimum criteria, provide general comments addressing the set of suggested questions in the guide. The template is a scaffold for minimum criteria and broader commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with rOpenSci packaging guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the package complies with the rOpenSci packaging guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly call out where it does and does not comply; reference specific packaging guide expectations when making recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code style and code patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate code style and code patterns; identify improvements that could be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instance, determine whether functions need to be broken down into smaller helper functions and whether the role of each helper function is clear. Offer concrete suggestions for clearer patterns and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce code duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and recommend reducing code duplication in the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out repeated logic that could be factored into a single helper or utility function, with examples of where consolidation would improve maintainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid replicating base R or lightweight dependency functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the package reimplements functionality already present in base R or in lightweight dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If functions in the package duplicate existing interfaces, suggest using existing base functions or lightweight dependencies instead of custom reimplementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface / API usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the user interface (function signatures, defaults, workflows) is clear and user-friendly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider improvements to the user-facing API; evaluate whether functions and arguments are named to work together to form a common, logical programming API that is easy to read and autocomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify possible performance improvements for the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out slow hotspots, inefficient algorithms, or opportunities to use vectorized operations or more efficient data structures; provide reproducible examples when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation clarity and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether documentation (installation instructions, vignettes, examples, demos) is clear and sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does the documentation use the principle of multiple points of entry (acknowledging any piece of documentation may be the user's first encounter)? Check vignette coverage, examples, and whether installation instructions work on a fresh system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple points of entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation should take into account that any piece may be a user's first encounter with the package or the tool/data it wraps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure there are tutorials, quick-start guides, and reference material so users at different familiarity levels can get started and find deeper docs as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming consistency for API
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether functions and arguments are named to form a common, logical programming API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names should be easy to read and autocomplete; check for inconsistent naming patterns and suggest harmonization to improve discoverability and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world/use-case testing by reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Work through the package with your own relevant data/problem to find rough edges and use-cases the author didn’t think about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing with a real problem can reveal surprising failure modes, missing functionality, or unclear behavior not apparent from examples alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful, kind tone and code of conduct adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality. Be respectful and kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rOpenSci code of conduct is mandatory for everyone involved in the review process. Offer constructive criticism and, where possible, suggest improvements or offer contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated tools in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated tools to facilitate your review (CI logs, package check reports, local checks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: check the package’s logs on CI (GitHub Actions, Codecov), run devtools::check() and devtools::test() locally to find errors missed on the author’s system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate skipped tests justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether tests’ skipping is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, distinguish between skip_on_cran tests that do real API requests (which may be justified) versus skipping all tests on one operating system (which may hide failures). Ask authors to justify skips where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect locally-built documentation (pkgdown may be stale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely solely on the package's hosted pkgdown site since it may not be up-to-date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend inspecting the package’s documentation locally by running pkgdown::build_site() to verify examples, vignettes, and reference documentation match the submitted code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regenerating checks via review bot
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may re-generate package check results from @ropensci-review-bot at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue the single comment '@ropensci-review-bot check package' in the review issue to trigger a fresh package report and checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record off-thread interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you interact with the package authors outside the review thread, capture and/or link relevant elements in your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversations in chats, DMs, in-person, or in the project repository should be referenced or linked in the official review so the centralized record contains those outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and centralization
rubrics_metrics.description: When your review is complete, paste it as a comment into the package software-review issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional comments are welcome in the same issue. Reviews are expected to be an ongoing conversation rather than a single round; if you submit issues or pull requests directly to the package repo, comment about them and link them in the software-review repo comment thread so there is a centralized record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include time estimate for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an estimate of how many hours you spent on your review afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps editors and the project understand reviewer effort and manage workload expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and approval workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should respond within 2 weeks with changes; reviewers should respond on whether changes sufficiently address issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage ongoing discussion between authors and reviewers, and ask editors to clarify issues in the review thread as needed. Use the provided approval template when approving changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pkgreviewr helper for workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Optionally streamline your review workflow with the pkgreviewr package (RStudio-friendly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage: install remotes::install_github('ropensci-org/pkgreviewr'), then pkgreview_create(pkg_repo = 'owner/repo', review_parent = '...') which clones the repo and creates a review project containing a notebook and the review template. Note: if not on the default branch, switch to the submitted branch after cloning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer appropriately and through correct channels
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to volunteer as a reviewer, fill the volunteering form and contact the editor by email for specific submissions rather than using the GitHub interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the package name, URL to the submission issue and the name of the assigned editor when emailing. Do not volunteer for all issues and respect editor discretion in reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning from example reviews and prior experience
rubrics_metrics.description: First-time reviewers should read past reviews and blog posts to understand review depth and approaches (e.g., 'naive user' testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of prior reviews and blog posts are provided; reviewers need not produce reviews as long as some examples but can alternate between using the package and checking its code to provide valuable feedback. If you can contribute code improvements, offer them.
